topics.title: Inequalities and Regions
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Identify and use inequality symbols. (k, s)
Illustrate inequalities on the number line. (u, s)
Solve linear inequalities in one unknown. (u, s)
Represent linear inequalities graphically. (k, u, s)
Form simple linear inequalities for regions on a graph. (u, s)

body.text: The inequality symbols are: > (greater than), < (less than), >= (greater than or equal to), and <= (less than or equal to). On a number line, a filled (solid) circle marks a value that is included (>= or <=), and an open circle marks a value that is excluded (> or <).

Linear inequalities in one unknown solve like equations, with one key difference: multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Solve 2x + 3 < 11: subtract 3 from both sides to get 2x < 8, then divide both sides by 2 to get x < 4.
Solve -3x + 2 <= 14: subtract 2 to get -3x <= 12, then divide by -3 — since -3 is negative, the inequality flips — giving x >= -4.

body.expr: -3x + 2 <= 14   ->   -3x <= 12   ->   x >= -4   (sign flips on dividing by a negative)

body.text: On a coordinate grid, an inequality like y > x + 1 defines a region rather than a single line. Draw the boundary line y = x + 1 (dashed, since y = x+1 itself is not included because the inequality is strict), then shade the side of the line where y is greater than x + 1 — check with a test point such as (0, 0): since 0 is not greater than 0+1=1, (0,0) is on the excluded side.
